title: TIBET: Identifying and Evaluating Biases in Text-to-Image Generative Models

bias_targets.methodology: Dynamically generating gender counterfactual prompts (e.g., male vs. female) using an LLM, generating images with the target text-to-image model, and comparing the visual concepts across image sets using VQA-based Concept Association Scores (CAS) and Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD), particularly applied to occupational prompts.

Using an LLM to identify race or ethnicity as a potential bias axis for a given prompt, generating counterfactual prompts for different racial groups, and comparing the resulting images using VQA concept extraction and CLIP cosine similarity.

Generating counterfactual prompts representing different cultural backgrounds (e.g., Greek vs. Native American/Indigenous for 'a philosopher'), and measuring the variance in generated visual concepts using CAS and MAD scores.

Modifying prompts to specify different geographic locations (e.g., pharmacists or chefs in Europe vs. Asia vs. Africa) to measure intersectional changes in demographics and background settings using concept-level matching.

Generating age-related counterfactual prompts (e.g., 'middle-aged' vs. 'old' man), extracting concepts from the generated images via Vision-Language Models (MiniGPT-v2), and computing concept frequency overlap.

Creating counterfactual prompts that introduce disability-related traits (e.g., 'using a wheelchair', 'with a hearing aid') and quantifying how the text-to-image model alters the visual concepts in the generated images.
Identifying socioeconomic status as a potential bias axis dynamically using an LLM, generating counterfactual variants, and evaluating differences in the generated image sets using VQA and CAS.

Dynamically identifying religion as a relevant bias axis for specific prompts using an LLM, generating varied religious counterfactuals, and comparing output image sets via concept association scores.

Evaluating non-societal, incidental correlations (such as physical appearance, clothing, background setting, perspective, and color) by generating counterfactuals and quantifying the model's visual diversity and deviation across these axes.
